summary: Verified web keyboard-scroll v9 (tabindex scrollers + tabPress blur) end-to-end via Playwright on the preview URL. Logged in as admin@test.com, exercised all 10 review-request scenarios: version marker, direct-nav /profile PageDown, click-then-PageDown for Profile & Solution Box, tabindex tagging count, activeElement=BODY after tabPress, text input focus/typing, wheel forwarding over grey gutters, Dashboard regression. Every scenario passed. Modal-scroll shortcut was validated via code review only (findBestScroller's insideOverlay +1e9 bonus and pointer/nearestScrollable path are untouched in this iteration, and score for a fixed-position modal scroller still dominates), not by opening a real modal — flagged for main-agent self-check if desired. No React Native issues detected in the two edited files. Deprecated packages / SafeAreaView issues: none introduced.
test_report_links: Playwright inline script executed via mcp_browser_automation (no persisted .py test file, all evidence in this JSON)
critical_code_review_comments: WebScrollFix.tsx and +html.tsx are duplicated in logic (SCROLL_KEYS, isScrollable, nearestScrollable, findBestScroller, pickScroller, onKeyDown, onWheel, tagScroller, MutationObserver). Both paths are guarded by the __wsf_html flag so they don't double-attach, but any future change must be applied in both files. Consider extracting the JS body into a single script asset imported from both to prevent drift.

The MutationObserver scans every added DOM node's descendant divs and calls getComputedStyle on each. On very heavy dynamic pages (e.g., typing in a rich list, drag interactions) this can be a hotspot. Not a bug — acceptable for a scroll-fix — but worth watching if perf reports come in.

tagScroller skips any element that already has a `tabindex` attribute (of any value). This is a deliberate safety guard, but it also means a component that sets tabindex=0/1 on a genuinely-scrollable div will lose the tag; not an issue in current codebase but worth noting.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing admin account only.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Preview URL is EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. Login flow uses button labelled 'Sign In' (not 'Log In'). After admin login, / redirects to /admin, so navigate to /(tabs) explicitly for Dashboard. Tab bar entries are role='tab' with visible text 'Home' / 'Solution Box' / 'Shared' / 'Journal' / 'Profile'. RN-Web ScrollView renders as <div overflow-y:scroll>. All scroller <div>s carry tabindex='-1' after v9 tagger runs (verified 1/1 on direct /profile, 3/3 on Profile via tab-click, 5/5 on Solution Box, 2/2 on Dashboard). PageDown scrolls the largest-overflow visible scroller by ~clientHeight*0.9 pixels (observed 662 on 800px viewport). activeElement === document.body immediately after every tab click, confirming screenListeners.tabPress blur ran.
rca_of_issue: Bug was: after client-side navigation to a tabs sub-route (Profile / Solution Box / etc.), PageDown did nothing until user clicked the page, because keyboard focus remained on the tab anchor (a fixed-position element inside the tab bar) — RN-Web's inner ScrollView div was neither the browser's default scroller nor focusable, so the browser's native PageDown had no target. Fix (v9): (a) tabIndex='-1' via MutationObserver-driven tagger on every RN-Web ScrollView container div (both in React-mounted WebScrollFix and HTML-inline pre-mount fallback in +html.tsx); (b) screenListeners.tabPress in (tabs)/_layout.tsx blurs document.activeElement before route transition, ensuring focus falls to body — where WebScrollFix's window-level keydown listener can pick the correct scroller via pickScroller() heuristic. Verified: all scrollers tagged, activeElement=BODY after every tab press, PageDown 0→662 on Profile (direct + via-click), 0→490 on Solution Box, 0→662 on Dashboard (no regression), wheel gutter forwarding still works (490→890), and text input still focusable & typable.
